summary:
Our project, Abandoned but Not Forgotten, is an interactive storytelling concept that explores NASA's equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. We developed an educational experience in which an AI robot guide named COSMOS takes students on a virtual space journey to discover the stories of the Apollo Lunar Rover, Sojourner, Spirit, and Opportunity.

The project addresses the challenge of limited awareness about abandoned space equipment by presenting its history, mission objectives, challenges, and scientific discoveries in an engaging and easy-to-understand format. We also propose an artifact database with images and details, interactive maps of the Moon and Mars, and digital storytelling features.

This project is important because abandoned equipment is not just waste; it represents humanity's achievements, scientific progress, and contribution to space exploration. Our goal is to make space history more accessible, interactive, and interesting for future generations.
details:
Users pick a machine on the map, read or hear its story, rotate its 3D model, and test themselves with a short quiz.

It makes learning fun and simple for school-age kids, and every fact is sourced from NASA.

To spark curiosity in space science and help students remember real missions through stories instead of dry facts

Languages like HTML/CSS/JavaScript, NASA images from images.nasa.gov, a 3D viewer, an AI assistant for drafting and research like Chat GPT, Gemini and Claude are used.

The machines narrate their own biographies, so history feels like a personal story. Status badges (Silent, Still working, Waiting) add an emotional arc.

Accuracy (NASA sources), age-appropriate language, short readable stories, clear visuals with image credits, and an easy design for phones.
